findings.issue: `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` everywhere — the legacy segment-config rendering model that Next 16.4 (2026-10-06) superseded with Cache Components and that Next 17 makes incompatible
findings.suggestion: Enable `cacheComponents: true` in next.config.mjs, delete all seven segment-config exports, and rely on dynamic-by-default data fetching (Next 16.4's recommended model)

findings.issue: `cache: 'no-store'` on every fetch is part of the same legacy opt-out caching interface that Cache Components replaces
findings.suggestion: Under Cache Components, plain fetch is dynamic by default; drop the cache option and use `use cache`/`cacheLife` selectively for the immutable lists (species, types, generations)

findings.issue: Inline duplicate of the idFromUrl regex already maintained in app/lib/format.js:48 — the two copies can drift

findings.suggestion: Move a shared `firstParam(params, key)` into lib/format.js or lib/search-params.js

findings.issue: Reads `window.location.search` directly to build filter URLs, a second URL-param pattern alongside the correct `useSearchParams()` used in MovesSection.jsx:31
findings.suggestion: Use `useSearchParams()` so all query-string handling goes through one primitive

findings.issue: Not-found handling is hand-rolled (catch-all route + inline component), so unknown URLs render with HTTP 200 and bypass the framework's convention
findings.suggestion: Call `notFound()` from 'next/navigation' after a missing resource and add `app/not-found.jsx`; remove the catch-all

findings.issue: Multi-request dynamic data path with no `error.jsx` or `loading.jsx`; an API hiccup surfaces the framework's default error page
findings.suggestion: Add route-level error/loading boundaries (or Suspense boundaries if adopting Cache Components)

findings.issue: Entirely untyped codebase against an external JSON API; 0 type lines at the data boundary
findings.suggestion: At minimum, type the API response shapes in lib/api.js so spec/API drift is caught at build time

findings.issue: `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` comment but no ESLint is installed or configured (empty devDependencies)
findings.suggestion: Either add the standard Next ESLint config or remove the dead directive

summary: A clean, dependency-minimal app on the current stable framework release that correctly adopts Next 16's breaking-change APIs. Its main forward-looking weakness is the rendering strategy: `force-dynamic` segment configs and `cache: 'no-store'` fetches on every route are the exact legacy model Next 16.4 replaced with Cache Components, so a Next 17 upgrade will ripple through all seven routes. Secondary duplication of URL/param/parsing helpers will cause drift over time, though data access itself is nicely isolated behind lib/api.js.

apis.replacement: Cache Components (`cacheComponents: true`, dynamic-by-default fetching, `use cache`/`cacheLife` for opted-in caching) — recommended for all apps since Next 16.4, default in create-next-app, incompatible with segment configs when enabled
Under Cache Components plain fetch is dynamic by default; use `use cache` for the immutable lists
